articles.title: Declining solar, storage valuations drive increased M&A: Mercom
articles.summary: “When there is uncertainty, there are good deals to be had,” said Mercom CEO Raj Prabhu. “People are looking for late-stage, low-risk projects that are ready to go, and those are hot commodities.”

articles.title: The physics of reliability: Why gas peakers alone can’t save the modern grid
articles.summary: Most outages don’t start as a multihour energy shortage; they start as a frequency crisis. If you only have gas, you’re trying to stop a bullet with a shield that takes 10 minutes to lift, writes Arun Muthukrishnan from Arevon Energy.

articles.title: Data centers remain standout industry for Schneider Electric
articles.summary: Data center orders accelerated toward the end of 2025 and will likely remain strong through 2026 as projects planned for the next 18 to 24 months take shape, Schneider Electric Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said.

articles.title: Tariffs drove construction input prices up to start 2026
articles.summary: January’s cost increases amounted to a “blistering” annualized rate of 7.1% for nonresidential input prices, according to Associated Builders and Contractors. Copper was up 80% year over year, iron and steel 58% and switchgear 67%.

articles.title: Addressing utility payment delinquencies amid rising energy burden
articles.summary: Rising payment delinquencies are putting pressure on utility revenue cycles. Utilities are adopting preventive strategies to stabilize cash flow and support customers.

articles.title: Sunrun installation volumes fall in Q4 2025 as VPP capacity grows
articles.summary: Executives with the largest provider of residential solar and battery subscriptions in the U.S. said regulatory uncertainty and a business model shift impacted 2025 volumes and its 2026 outlook.

articles.title: Virginia, Indiana lawmakers pass surplus interconnection bills
articles.summary: Using existing surplus interconnection, such as at rarely-used peaker plants, can get generation and storage resources online faster and more cheaply than seeking new interconnection rights. PJM lags behind other grid operators in pursuing this.

articles.title: CARB approves California’s climate disclosure regulations
articles.summary: The California Air Resources Board, tasked with enforcing the state’s climate disclosure laws, will require companies to report Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by August this year.

articles.title: PJM proposes fast-track interconnection plan, capacity auction price collar
articles.summary: The PJM Interconnection says it is taking steps to bring new generation online as fast as possible while protecting ratepayers from high capacity prices.

articles.title: OpenStar demonstrates dipole fusion reactor concept
articles.summary: New Zealand-based fusion energy startup OpenStar Technologies says it has become the first commercial company in the world to successfully create and confine plasma using a levitated dipole reactor.

articles.title: Czech-Korean ministerial committee established for Dukovany project
articles.summary: A ministerial steering committee has been established to oversee progress on the Dukovany new nuclear project - as significant new contracts have been signed between South Korean and Czech companies.

articles.title: Blue Capsule begins building sodium test loop
articles.summary: French small modular reactor developer Blue Capsule Technology has announced the start of construction of ELISE - a full-size test rig for sodium at high temperatures - at Peyrolles-en-Provence, in collaboration with France's CSTI Groupe.

articles.title: TVONS to provide advice for Estonian SMR project
articles.summary: Finnish consulting company TVO Nuclear Services and Estonia's Fermi Energia have signed a framework agreement under which TVONS will act as a consultant in Fermi Energia's small modular reactor power plant project in Estonia.

articles.title: Slovenia moves ahead with new nuclear planning
articles.summary: Prime Minister Robert Golob said that by the time the postponed referendum on a new unit at the Krško Nuclear Power Plant is held, the location of the new block will be known, as well as the likely cost of the project and the technology to be used.

articles.title: US microreactor transported by air
articles.summary: A Valar Atomics microreactor has been transported on a US Air Force cargo plane from California to Utah and will eventually be moved to the Utah San Rafael Energy Lab for testing and evaluation.

articles.title: Croatia aims for 30% nuclear energy by 2040
articles.summary: The Croatian government has sent a draft law on the development of nuclear energy to the country's parliament.

articles.title: Russian regulator issues operating licence for second Zaporizhzhia unit
articles.summary: Rostekhnadzor has issued a 10-year operating licence for Unit 2 at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, which has been under Russian military control since early March 2022.

articles.title: Construction phase completed in Bruce 3 refurbishment
articles.summary: Bruce Power has completed the construction phase of its Unit 3 Major Component Replacement project, which it says remains on budget and ahead of schedule.

articles.title: US seeks to boost nuclear energy ties in Slovakia, Hungary
articles.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio has announced measures to promote nuclear projects using US technology in Slovakia and Hungary.

articles.title: Illinois governor aims to speed up nuclear new-build
articles.summary: An executive order has been issued by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker that will support the deployment of new nuclear facilities in the US state. He said his goal is "delivering at least two gigawatts of new clean nuclear capacity".

articles.title: Copenhagen Atomics secures thorium supply from Norway
articles.summary: Denmark's Copenhagen Atomics has signed a Letter of Intent with Rare Earths Norway to secure future access to thorium - the key fertile material in its molten salt reactor technology - extracted from the Fensfeltet deposit in Norway.

articles.title: TerraPower's Natrium reactor enters UK GDA process
articles.summary: The Bill Gates-chaired company's Natrium 345 MWe sodium-cooled fast reactor with a molten-salt-based energy storage system has been accepted into the UK's Generic Design Assessment process.

articles.title: Denison granted licence for Wheeler River
articles.summary: The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission has issued a licence to Denison Mines Corp to prepare a site and construct a uranium mine and mill at its Wheeler River project in Saskatchewan. The project is the first uranium mine in Canada to use the in-situ recovery mining method.

articles.title: Urenco installs innovative heat network at Dutch site
articles.summary: Uranium enrichment services provider Urenco has broken ground for a new net-zero project at its facility in Almelo in the Netherlands that will recycle waste heat from the enrichment process.

articles.title: Kairos, DOE enhance collaboration on advanced reactor design
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Kairos Power have entered into a USD27 million strategic partnership to accelerate the technology needed to deploy a new generation of advanced nuclear reactors.

articles.title: Reactor vessel installed at Lufeng 6
articles.summary: The reactor pressure vessel has been hoisted into place at unit 6 of the Lufeng nuclear power plant in China's Guangdong province. It is the second of two HPR1000 (Hualong One) units under construction at the site, where four CAP1000s are also planned.

articles.title: Serbia and Russia discuss nuclear energy cooperation
articles.summary: Serbian Energy Minister Dubravka Đedović Handanović says that the country - already cooperating with France's EDF on the preparations for a nuclear energy programme - "is ready to establish cooperation with other technology providers from whom we can learn".

articles.title: Environmental approval for Saskatchewan uranium project
articles.summary: Australia-headquartered Paladin Energy Limited has received approval from the Government of Saskatchewan for its Environmental Impact Statement for development of its Patterson Lake South project, located in the Athabasca Basin, Canada.

articles.title: Canada to offer training as part of IAEA Rays of Hope initiative
articles.summary: The Canadian Nuclear Isotope Council is planning training programmes for low- and middle-income countries in areas such as radiation safety and isotope production as part of the International Atomic Energy Agency's cancer-tackling Rays of Hope programme.
